children: SAN FRANCISCO — The Saudi national accused of bugging an OpenAI conference room was ordered released from jail on $1 million bond pending trial, after a judge determined the former OpenAI engineer didn't present an immediate flight risk.

Abdulrahman Alfozan, who pleaded not guilty this month to recording oral communications, will have to wear an ankle monitor to track his location as a condition of his release, will be restricted from leaving Northern California, U.S. Magistrate Judge Alex G. Tse ruled Tuesday.
Alfozan is set to be released on Wednesday morning from Santa Clara jail, and stay at home in Millbrae., Calif., with his trial set to begin in January.

Federal prosecutors allege that the 35-year-old Alfozan spent weeks in September collecting secret recordings at OpenAI, using the company's AI tools to help put together inexpensive recording devices that captured conversations in conference rooms, including meetings with OpenAI customers and government officials.
Alfozan was arrested in early October after one of the devices was discovered wrapped in toilet paper behind a wall-mounted conference-room television set in late September.

Federal prosecutors have argued that Alfozan should be held without bail over concerns he would flee to Saudi Arabia. They allege he has been in contact with Saudi officials, including a member of the royal family, about jobs in the kingdom.
Updates to follow as news develops.
